key_insight: Instead of sending messages as tokens, agentic LLMs can compile their intermediate activations into transient parameter updates (weight patches) that are applied to receivers — enabling richer, cheaper inter-agent communication. This lets agents share computation directly without serializing everything into text.
problem_solved: Token-based message passing between LLM agents forces senders' intermediate computation to be re-encoded and reprocessed by receivers, driving up generated-token cost, prefill overhead, KV-cache memory, and latency.
method: Compile a sender's hidden states into a compact, transient parameter update (e.g., low-rank adapter or delta-weights) instead of appending verbal messages to the context.

Transmit the lightweight weight patch to the receiver and apply it transiently so the receiver continues inference with the sender's computation embedded, avoiding re-tokenization and extra KV-cache entries.
Design the patch to be scoped/ephemeral and compatibility-calibrated (projection or adapter interface) to preserve model stability and enable rollback.
impact: This approach cuts token-generation and KV-cache costs, lowers latency, and enables more expressive and efficient multi-agent collaboration — useful for building scalable, cost-effective agent networks and modular model stacks.

paper_title: Good Agentic Friends Do Not Just Give Verbal Advice: They Can Update Your Weights
paper_authors: Wenrui Bao, Huan Wang, Jian Wang, Zhangyang Wang, Kai Wang
